title: Spruce Labs intake and staging roadmap
summary: Kickoff to align on Spruce Labs staging topology, data residency constraints, and rollout milestones for Redwood Private. Agreed next steps: run a small bench on a staging VPC, share security pack, and schedule cluster provisioning call. Discussed prefix caching, model pinning, and canary strategy.
topics: dedicated vs hosted decision for pilot
action_items: Maya - send security pack (SOC2 + audit logs + KMS integration details) - due 2027-12-03
Liam - prepare a short bench script and token/cost estimate for 1 week pilot - due 2027-12-06
Carlos - confirm VPC CIDR, peering and egress constraints, and share with Redwood - due 2027-12-02
Aisha - provide sample payloads and SLA targets (p95 latency, throughput needs) - due 2027-12-04
next_steps: Provision staging environment and run bench
Follow-up provisioning call to walk through VPC peering and subnets (week of 12/6)
Agree pilot acceptance criteria and go/no-go window (2-week pilot suggested)
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-12-01
- Start: 15:30 PST
- Duration: ~57 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood CSM), Liam (Redwood SE), Rajiv (Redwood oncall), Aisha (Spruce Head of MLOps), Carlos (Platform Lead), Meera (Eng Manager), Jon (Security)

Summary: quick intake to line up network and security items for staging + first pilot. Lots of questions on VPC egress and KMS, also some back-and-forth on whether to run Dedicated reserved or Private for the pilot.

Topics / Agenda: 1) High-level goals and timeline 2) Network/topology 3) Data residency & encryption 4) Bench and metrics 5) Next steps

00:00 Maya: okay good morning everyone, thanks for making time. this is the kickoff to get the staging and pilot lined up, i'll run through the agenda real quick and then Liam will do a quick tech intake.
00:12 Aisha: hey thanks Maya, we wanted to keep this tight, our Q1 production deadline is sort of soft but we need a pilot in our staging infra by mid-december so we can iterate.
00:22 Liam: great, i can cover the network requirements and the bench plan. quick check — are we leaning private deployment from the start? or do you want hosted for speed?
00:33 Carlos: we prefer private, mainly for compliance reasons — PII-ish logs, and needs to stay in our VPC. but budget is, uh, a little constrained so we're open to dedicated as an alternative if it's faster.
00:45 Meera: also curious about how much work on our side for KV cache / prefix caching setup, we do a lot of short queries across sessions.
00:53 Rajiv: small note — our runtime team can help with peering and routes but we need to know subnets and security groups ahead of provisioning.
01:05 Liam: okay, so high-level: Redwood Private can run in your VPC with a customer-managed control plane. we support KMS integrations — we saw Jon on the line, can we get your KMS provider?
01:16 Jon: we're on AWS KMS, multi-account. we'll need envelope encryption and audit logs, plus SAML SSO tied to our IdP.
01:24 Maya: perfect, i'll add those as items in the security pack — SOC2 evidence, KMS flow, SSO/SAML notes, and audit log retention options.
01:33 Aisha: can you clarify audit log retention? we need 7 years for a subset of logs for compliance, is that feasible?
01:40 Maya: long retention's an add-on, we'll note options — default is 90 days in the console, but we can arrange archived logs to your S3 with lifecycle rules. i'll include specifics.
01:50 Liam: back to topology — for staging we recommend a small three-node pool, GPU-backed, pinned to a mid-size quantized model to start. that'll give you predictable p95 latency while keeping cost manageable.
02:01 Carlos: can you give a rough token cost estimate for say 50k tokens/day over a week? just to budget.
02:07 Liam: we'll run a bench script that simulates your payloads; i'll produce a token/cost estimate. ballpark, with quantization and batching you might see 40-60% cost of a float model but i'll put numbers in the doc.
02:20 Meera: one more on caching — our queries are highly repetitive, will Redwood prefix or kv caching be automatic? or is that extra config?
02:29 Rajiv: sometimes the auto-caching needs a little help — you can enable prefix caching per-route, and we have a cache-ttl configuration. Liam?
02:35 Liam: yeah, automatic prefix caching is available but we need to map your request identifiers, sometimes field names get normalized differently. expect a small mapping task. we'll share an example mapping script.
02:47 Aisha: network specifics — we have restrictive egress rules, only certain endpoints allowed. is there a need for outbound to external repos or will it be contained?
02:55 Liam: for Private in-VPC, outbound is only for optional telemetry and auth calls. your control: we can route telemetry to your proxy or disable it. for initial pilot, we suggest allowing Redwood's control-plane endpoints to the specific CIDRs, but we can do peering-only flow.
03:12 Jon: from security perspective we prefer peering and no NAT egress. is that supported?
03:16 Rajiv: yep that's a supported pattern. we need the CIDRs and we'll provide the peering template.
03:22 Meera: great. can we also pin model versions? last time a model change broke our downstream parsing.
03:28 Liam: absolutely. model pinning and canary rollouts are supported. we can set a canary to sample X% traffic and then flip.
03:35 Aisha: what about rollback and automatic fallback — if a new model regresses on hallucination tests, do you have auto fallback?
03:42 Liam: we have a fallback policy at the routing layer — if production SLOs or a specified health check fails, traffic can route to a previous pinned model or a cheaper replica.
03:51 Carlos: bench details, how long do you need to run the pilot to get meaningful numbers? two weeks?
03:56 Liam: i'd say 7-14 days depending on traffic variance. for initial acceptance maybe 1 week of stable traffic plus a stress day.
04:06 Aisha: ok, timeline — we want pilot by mid-december; what do you need from us today to hit that?
04:12 Maya: short list — VPC details (CIDR, subnets, routes), KMS ARN, sample payloads, p95 targets, and stakeholder contacts. we'll also ask for a primary and backup contact for fast turnarounds.
04:24 Carlos: i'll share the VPC doc and ask infra to open a ticket for peering, aim to have that by tomorrow.
04:31 Maya: perfect. action items and ownership we'll email.
04:36 Meera: small question — are we going to be billed to our contract or run on a trial account for the pilot?
04:41 Maya: for pilots we usually set up a limited billing sandbox under your account or a trial credit depending on procurement; i'll include both paths in the email and link to pricing.
04:50 Jon: any red flags from Redwood side we should watch for?
04:54 Liam: just watch for tokenization differences if you have heavy multilingual payloads — sometimes sequence length changes costs. we'll instrument that in the bench.
05:02 Aisha: noted. also want to run an eval suite for hallucinations, can Redwood run prompt-specific regression tests during the pilot?
05:09 Liam: yes we can hook up your prompt set and run diffs across model versions; we'll include evaluation harness steps.
05:16 Maya: alright last bits — i'll send the security packet and the onboarding checklist after this call, Liam will attach the bench script, Carlos and Aisha will share the VPC and payloads. we should have provisioning in the week of 12/6.
05:30 Liam: sounds good, i'll also provide a sample canary config and the minimal IAM/role spec for the peering flow.
05:36 Maya: fantastic. thanks everyone, we'll follow-up with the calendar invite for the provisioning walk-through.
05:41 Aisha: thanks all, excited to get started.
05:44 Carlos: thanks, bye.

Post-call notes: minor transcription oddities — "K-V cache" transcribed literal, some proper nouns distorted (Spruce internal tool names), speaker labels occasionally overlapped. Important deliverables: security pack, bench script, VPC details, sample payloads.
